top_choice_rationale: P002 (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford) credits three separable originators of one mature framework. Taylor's staggered contracts, Calvo's tractable time-dependent pricing and Woodford's microfounded policy synthesis together underpin modern monetary-policy analysis. That work is 25 to 45 years old, has been through 2008 and the 2021-23 inflation by being modified and extended rather than abandoned, and has not been recognised directly by an earlier prize. Its breadth and durability of influence outweigh the cleaner two-name credit of P003 and P001, though I hold it with real doubts: eight names are credited on the ballot entry, any three-person cut omits contributors such as Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and Gertler, and micro evidence on state-dependent pricing qualifies Calvo's mechanism. I read the discovery as origination of the nominal-rigidity mechanisms and their policy synthesis, not the usable estimated framework. That is a contestable judgement, and the citation should be worded accordingly. P003 (Kiyotaki, Moore) is a clean, original and mature mechanism, distinct from the 2022 bank-run prize, but narrower in scope and less cleanly identified empirically. P001 (Melitz, Helpman) is distinct from the 2008 prize and well tested on firm-level data, but its credit boundary is unsettled because Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum are not credited. I rank all three above no award because each is a defensible prize on merit. Support counts did not enter my ranking.
recusal_note: Profile-based disclosures, not adjudicated: I co-author with committee members Krusell, Boppart and Friberg and am an IIES colleague of Krusell and Boppart, and none of them is a candidate. My menu-cost research with Friberg and Ellingsen is close to the nominal-rigidities literature in P002 but is not work by Calvo, Taylor or Woodford. The 2018 Scientific Background cites my own work, which does not concern any proposal on this slate. No collaboration or institutional tie to Calvo, Taylor, Woodford, Kiyotaki, Moore, Melitz or Helpman is apparent from my profile.
